tagline: Across the Big Scrub, where the bears keep near the road.
intro: SR 40 leaves Silver Springs and runs east 60 miles to I-95, through the Ocala National Forest, the oldest national forest east of the Mississippi, with loops and spurs reaching off it. Around it lies the Big Scrub, ancient sand dunes long since grown over, the largest continuous sand pine forest left in Florida.

Florida black bears live thicker here than anywhere else and are often seen close to the road. Several springs lie along the way. The road crosses the St. Johns River at Astor, between Lake George and Lake Dexter, and comes out past Barberville to the interstate.

moments.title: Silver Springs
moments.text: The glass-bottom boat was invented here in the late 1870s, and the springs at the head of the Silver River later served as a location for several Tarzan films.

moments.title: Salt Springs
moments.text: A swimming hole in the national forest holds at 72 degrees all year. It is full of bass, turtles and blue crabs, and runs out to Lake George.

moments.title: Astor
moments.text: On the St. Johns, William Backhouse Astor Jr. bought more than 12,000 acres in 1874 and laid out a town he called Manhattan, its settlers arriving by steamboat. The name never caught on.
